@commonCancel.description: Closes a dialog or question without doing anything.

@commonFilter.description: A search field's label and placeholder.

@commonMessage.description: A commit, tag or stash message field.

@refsDeletedBranch.description: The branches view's bar, after a branch was deleted; commit is a short hash.

@refsRestore.description: A button: makes the branches just deleted again.

@refsCleanUp.description: A button: lists the branches that can be deleted.

@refsName.description: The field for a new remote's name.

@refsInWorktree.description: After a branch's name: the folder of the other worktree it is checked out in.

@refsOnBranch.description: After a branch's name: the branch it is stacked on.

@refsTagKindLightweight.description: A column of the tag list: the kind of tag.

@refsTagKindAnnotated.description: A column of the tag list: the kind of tag.

@refsTagKindSigned.description: A column of the tag list: the kind of tag.

@refsCheckOut.description: A verb: checks out a branch, tag or submodule.

refsPushStack: {count, plural, one {Push Stack of # Branch} other {Push Stack of # Branches}}
refsSwitchMessage: Carried changes stay in the files; git stops if one would be overwritten. Stashed changes go to the stash list.
refsDeleteBranchesMessage: Each is backed up first; Undo brings it back.
refsDeleteBranchesWorktreesMessage: Each is backed up first; Undo brings it back. The worktree at {folders} is removed with its branch; git refuses if it has changes.

@refsDeleteBranchesWorktreesMessage.description: folders is a comma-separated list of paths.

@refsRestoreBranchJob.description: The name of a write in the activity list.

@refsPushTo.description: A submenu of a tag's menu, listing the remotes.

refsDeleteTagMessage: Only here; a tag already pushed stays on the remote. Undo brings it back.

@refsFetch.description: A verb: a menu button and a remote's menu item.

@refsPull.description: A verb: the menu button of the ways to pull.

@refsPush.description: A verb: a menu button and its first item.

refsForcePushMessage: Only if it is still where this repository last fetched it; otherwise nothing is pushed.

@refsPushURL.description: Under a remote's URL: the other URL it pushes to.

@refsChange.description: A button: sets the remote's URL.

refsRemoveRemoteMessage: Its remote-tracking branches go with it; the remote itself is not touched.

@refsUpstreamGone.description: A branch's tracking column: its upstream branch was deleted on the remote.

@refsWhyMerged.description: Why a branch can be deleted; several are joined by commas.

@refsWhyRebased.description: Why a branch can be deleted; several are joined by commas.

@refsWhySquashed.description: Why a branch can be deleted; several are joined by commas.

@refsWhyUpstreamGone.description: Why a branch can be deleted; several are joined by commas.

@refsCleanupAgainst.description: Before the menu of the branch the others are compared with.

pullsNoCLI: Pull requests need GitHub's gh or GitLab's glab, logged in; neither was found on the PATH

@pullsDraft.description: After a pull request's number: it is a draft.

pullsOpen: {kind, select, gitlab {Open Merge Request {ref}} other {Open Pull Request {ref}}}

@pullsOpen.description: kind is gitlab for GitLab, else GitHub; ref is the request's number, as #12 or !12.

pullsShowInBrowser: {kind, select, gitlab {Show Merge Requests in Browser} other {Show Pull Requests in Browser}}
pullsCreateInBrowser: {kind, select, gitlab {Create Merge Request in Browser} other {Create Pull Request in Browser}}

@pullsStackPosition.description: After a branch's name: its place in a GitHub stack.

pullsStackBranch: Branch {index} of {count} in a GitHub stack
pullsStackBranchNumber: Branch {index} of {count} in a GitHub stack, #{number, number, ::group-off}
pullsSubmitStackMessage: {count, plural, one {gh stack pushes the # branch of the stack and creates or updates their pull requests on GitHub; new ones are drafts.} other {gh stack pushes the # branches of the stack and creates or updates their pull requests on GitHub; new ones are drafts.}}

@pullsSubmitStackJob.description: The name of a write in the activity list.

@pullsPushStackJob.description: The name of a write in the activity list.

pullsCreateStackItem: {count, plural, one {Create GitHub Stack of # Branch…} other {Create GitHub Stack of # Branches…}}
pullsCreateStackMessage: gh stack makes a stack of {branches}, from the bottom, and checks out {top}.

@pullsCreateStackMessage.description: branches is a comma-separated list of branch names.

@pullsCreateStackJob.description: The name of a write in the activity list.

remoteCheckoutNotTracking: {name} does not track {remote}; resetting it drops what it has that {remote} does not.
remoteCheckoutSame: {name} is at the same commit as {remote}.
remoteCheckoutBehind: {count, plural, one {{name} is # commit behind {remote}.} other {{name} is # commits behind {remote}.}}
remoteCheckoutAhead: {count, plural, one {{name} is # commit ahead of {remote}, not pushed.} other {{name} is # commits ahead of {remote}, not pushed.}}
remoteCheckoutDiverged: {name} and {remote} have diverged: {ahead, plural, one {# commit} other {# commits}} ahead, {behind, plural, one {# commit} other {# commits}} behind.
remoteCheckoutResetNote: A reset backs up {name} first; Undo brings it back.
remoteCheckoutElsewhereTitle: Branch {name} is checked out in another worktree
remoteCheckoutElsewhereMessage: git checks out a branch in one worktree at a time. It is checked out at {folder}.

@remoteCheckoutOpen.description: A button: opens the other worktree; folder is its folder's name.

@submoduleNotCheckedOutLabel.description: A submodule in the sidebar that is not checked out.

@submoduleUpdate.description: A verb: checks out the commit the repository records for the submodule.

submoduleCheckOutMessage: Check Out clones it from its URL and checks out the commit this repository records, with its own submodules.
